title: Pitched and hipped roofs from overlapping sagging strips with eave overhang
note: A roof is overlapping strips per slope plus a ridge; one plane reads as a plank and a flat top as a grey box.
intent: A single roof plane reads as "plank-like", and a flat top turns distant massing into "stepped grey boxes". Every building gets a roof form (pitched or hipped) built from ≥ 5 overlapping strips per slope, each strip drooping 5–10° more than the one above it and overhanging the eave by ≥ 0.15 units, with a ridge line that sags rather than runs straight (mid-span dip 5–10% of span; sagging thatch dips 10–15%). Thatch needs ≥ 4 overlapping sagging strip rows before it stops reading as flat plank. No two adjacent houses share width, height and roof pitch, and each strip carries its own value jitter so the slope does not tile.

check.note: Every tagged roof is built from >= 5 overlapping strips per slope (>= 10 per pitched roof) plus a ridge object; a single roof plane reads as plank-like and a flat top as a grey box.

port: Call makeHippedRoof(w, d, pitch) from the buildings facet for every house and background mass, tag the group "roof", strips "roof-strip" and the ridge "ridge"; keep strip count, overlap and per-strip sag as numbers in the brief. Fade distant roofs with fog rather than flattening them to boxes.

evidence.note: thatch/roof planes need ≥5 overlapping strips per slope, each drooping 5–10° more than the one above, overhanging the eave ≥0.15 units; distant massing needs a pitched/hipped roof form, not a flat top
sagging non-straight roof ridge line per house; no two adjacent houses share width/height/roof-pitch
ridge mid-span dip 5–10% of span; thatch is a fail until ≥4 overlapping sagging strip rows
sagging thatch ridge dips 10–15% at mid-span; layered elements must specify strip count, overlap depth and per-strip sag
